summary: feat(core/inference): split unusable responses from corruption — a response that completed (its terminal event arrived) but whose assembled payload violates the request contract now raises inference.ProviderResponseUnusable, classified NotAvailable and attempt-void at caller granularity like ProviderTruncated and never auto-retried (it joins the route's nonRetryableKind list), while wire-level corruption keeps InvalidProviderResponse; a part that cannot be assembled after the terminal finish event (stream.finish.part) is the unusable kind too, decode, normalize and accumulation failures in flight stay corruption, and the transcription session classifies its terminal violation through the same constructor as its unary sibling. The `inference route failed` warn line gains error.cause, carrying the leaf cause message of the first inference-owned cause beneath the outer error (response-validation checks, undefined-tool rejections, tool-call conflicts) when that message is redacted by construction: inference.CauseMessage walks the chain, driver, transport and context causes stay out, and what may appear in the attribute is bounded — tool names and media types render through quoteToken (quoted, rune-aware truncation at 64 runes) — with the redactedCause and core/telemetry.AttrErrorCause contracts spelling out the three sources they allow, the JSON-schema and encoding/json renderers behind the structured-output checks included. core/tool/mcp gives up on a command the OS cannot start: connectError maps exec.ErrNotFound, fs.ErrPermission, ENOENT, EACCES and ENOEXEC on the path form to Validation, the category retryLoop already gives up on, so a stdio server whose command is missing, not executable or not a runnable file stops backing off against a binary that will never exist, while a failure outside that set (a fork the kernel refused for lack of resources, say) stays retryable and a refused dial is still NotAvailable; the give-up notifies the new mcp.WithServerLost(func(server string, err error)) once with the failure — transient losses stay silent, so a server that reconnects keeps its tools and a self-healing plugin cannot flap an observer — WaitReady fails fast for a server a host marked required instead of paying the full timeout, hosts that only need to know a server is up keep using WithRequired plus WaitReady, and the give-up telemetry says "cannot connect" rather than "rejected" because the command may never have started.
